summary: Lakeba Island Airport is a small regional airstrip serving Lakeba, one of the principal islands in Fiji's remote Lau archipelago. The airport provides a vital air link between this eastern island group and the rest of Fiji, handling small turboprop aircraft on short, scenic flights. Its isolated Pacific location and minimal infrastructure make it one of the more off-the-beaten-path gateways in the country.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly to Lakeba Island Airport?
A: Fiji Link operates scheduled turboprop services connecting Lakeba with Suva, typically via stops at other Lau islands. Flights are limited and subject to weather conditions.

Q: How long is the runway at LKB?
A: The airport has a single short runway suitable only for small aircraft such as the ATR 72 or similar regional turboprops.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport?
A: Facilities are very basic, reflecting the airport's small size. There is a simple terminal building but limited amenities, so travelers should bring their own supplies.

Q: Do I need a permit to visit Lakeba?
A: As part of Fiji's Lau Islands, visitors may need special permits or arrangements through local authorities or tour operators, depending on current regulations.
transport_tips: Ground transport from the airport is informal; arrange a ride with your hotel or a local contact in advance, as taxis are not reliably available. Most accommodations on Lakeba offer airport pickup services. The airport is a short distance from the main village of Tubou, but roads are limited and a vehicle or boat transfer is often needed.
local_tip: Pack light and bring cash in Fijian dollars, as there are no ATMs on Lakeba and card acceptance is uncommon outside major guesthouses.
